paragraphs: Monmouthshire County Council's fostering service is Foster Wales Monmouthshire, one of the 22 council services in the not-for-profit Foster Wales network, based at County Hall in Usk. It sits within the council's children's services, so carers work closely with the social workers who know each child. Children from Abergavenny, Monmouth, Chepstow, Caldicot and Usk are looked after by its carers and by the services shown above.

The council says carers have a dedicated, qualified social worker, a personal learning record and development plan, out-of-hours help, a buddy, peer support groups and a group of experienced carers known as Pioneers. Its BASE service gives psychology and therapy support to children in care, and its MyST scheme looks after children with the most complex needs, with specialist training, enhanced fees and support around the clock. A peer group called Men who Care supports male carers.

Foster Wales Monmouthshire pays an allowance to cover a child's costs and a separate fee whose level depends on your skills and experience; it does not publish the amounts on these pages. Writing in 2023, the council said that across Wales most children placed with private agencies lived outside their home area, while most with council carers stayed local.

Foster Wales's national guide sets the minimum weekly allowance for 2026-27 at around £229 for children under four up to £260 for young people over 16. Our Wales page explains how children's care in Wales is moving to councils and not-for-profit providers, and our Newport page covers the neighbouring city. Ask Foster Wales Monmouthshire and one or two of the services above what they pay and how they support their carers.
